imageRy: A Statistical Framework for Exploring Spectral Imagery

<!-- Alternative title: From Pixels to Distributions: A New Way to Visualize Raster Data in R -->

Duccio Rocchini

Alma Mater Studiorum University of Bologna, Italy

<br> <!-- linee vuote html -->

Presentation held online at:



The problem

Why this matters for raster data

Current gap

Distribution plots are common in R:

ggplot2

ggridges

ggdist

plotly

But they are mostly designed for tabular data.

Raster users often need custom scripts to convert rasters into data frames before visualization.

Aim of the framework

Create a unified workflow for distribution-based visualization of geographical rasters directly in R.

The framework is implemented in the open-source package:

imageRy

available at: https://github.com/ducciorocchini/imageRy

Outline of the workflow

Four complementary functions

Function

Purpose

im.levelplot()

Visualize raster layers distributions

im.ridgeline()

Compare distributions among raster layers

im.boxplot.layers()

Compare medians, spread and densities among layers

im.boxplot.classes()

Compare distributions among spatial classes

1. Spatial exploration

Spatial exploration by im.levelplot()

{r, echo=T, eval=F}
im.levelplot(blet, layer = 3, custom_colors = "mako", margin = "median")

2. Layer-wise distribution exploration

Outline

Layer-wise distribution exploration

Empirical example: monthly NDVI

{r, echo=T}
library(terra)
ls <- list.files("~/Documents/ridgeline_plots/perduccio/ndvi", pattern = "\\.tif$",full.names = TRUE)
plot(ndvi <- rast(ls))

Ridgelines reveal the seasonal signal

{r, echo=T}
library(imageRy)
im.ridgeline(ndvi, scale=2, palette="viridis")

Names

{r, echo=T}
names(ndvi) <- c("01-Jan", "02-Feb", "03-Mar", "04-Apr", "05-May", "06-Jun", "07-Jul", "08-Aug", "09-Sep", "10-Oct", "11-Nov", "12-Dec") 
im.ridgeline(ndvi, scale=2, palette="viridis")

Scale

{r, echo=T}
names(ndvi) <- c("01-Jan", "02-Feb", "03-Mar", "04-Apr", "05-May", "06-Jun", "07-Jul", "08-Aug", "09-Sep", "10-Oct", "11-Nov", "12-Dec") 
im.ridgeline(ndvi, scale=4, palette="viridis")

2. Layer-wise statistical comparison

Outline

Layer-wise statistical comparison

Empirical example: species distribution spread (code)

{r, echo=T, eval=F}
# packages
library(terra)         # for SpatRaster and c()
library(virtualspecies)
library(imageRy)
library(geodata)
library(ggplot2)
library(viridis)

# climate (WorldClim v2.1 at 0.5 arc-min)
tmin <- worldclim_country("Lux", "tmin", path = tempdir(), res = 0.5, version = "2.1")
tmax <- worldclim_country("Lux", "tmax", path = tempdir(), res = 0.5, version = "2.1")
prec <- worldclim_country("Lux", "prec", path = tempdir(), res = 0.5, version = "2.1")

# July layers
tmin_jul <- tmin[[7]]
tmax_jul <- tmax[[7]]
prec_jul <- prec[[7]]

# environmental stack
env_stack_base <- c(tmin_jul, tmax_jul, prec_jul)
names(env_stack_base) <- c("tmin", "tmax", "prec")
summary(env_stack_base)

# 1) Species response curves consistent with the area's summary (tmin~12, tmax~22, prec~75):
#    - dec: prefers cooler & drier -> worsens with warming/wetting
#    - inc: prefers warmer & wetter -> improves with warming/wetting
#    - stab: broad tolerance around current values -> roughly stable
curve_list <- list(
  dec  = formatFunctions( # decreasing: slightly cooler/drier than 2000
    tmin = c(fun="dnorm", mean=11.5, sd=1.2),
    tmax = c(fun="dnorm", mean=21.0, sd=1.5),
    prec = c(fun="dnorm", mean=70,   sd=6)
  ),
  inc  = formatFunctions( # increasing: slightly warmer/wetter than 2000
    tmin = c(fun="dnorm", mean=13.5, sd=1.2),
    tmax = c(fun="dnorm", mean=24.0, sd=1.5),
    prec = c(fun="dnorm", mean=82,   sd=6)
  ),
  stab = formatFunctions( # stable: centered and tolerant
    tmin = c(fun="dnorm", mean=12.0, sd=3.5),
    tmax = c(fun="dnorm", mean=22.0, sd=3.5),
    prec = c(fun="dnorm", mean=75,   sd=12)
  )
)

# 2) Parametric climate change: default ~ +0.2 °C/year and +0.5 precip units/year
get_env_for_year <- function(year, base_stack,
                             dt_tmin = 0.2,  # °C/year
                             dt_tmax = 0.2,  # °C/year
                             dt_prec = 0.5   # precip units/year (same units as 'prec')
) {
  d <- year - 2000
  r <- if (inherits(base_stack, "SpatRaster")) base_stack else terra::rast(base_stack)
  r[["tmin"]] <- r[["tmin"]] + dt_tmin * d
  r[["tmax"]] <- r[["tmax"]] + dt_tmax * d
  r[["prec"]] <- r[["prec"]] + dt_prec * d
  r
}

# 3) Simulation: returns a stack per species (layers = years), values in [0,1]
simulate_three_species <- function(env_stack_base,
                                   years = 2000:2020,
                                   curves = curve_list,
                                   seed = 8888,
                                   dt_tmin = 0.2, dt_tmax = 0.2, dt_prec = 0.5,
                                   rescale = TRUE) {
  set.seed(seed)
  base_spat <- if (inherits(env_stack_base, "SpatRaster")) env_stack_base else terra::rast(env_stack_base)
  
  get_suit <- function(vs_obj) if (is.list(vs_obj) && "suitab.raster" %in% names(vs_obj)) vs_obj$suitab.raster else vs_obj
  
  out <- vector("list", length(curves))
  names(out) <- names(curves)
  
  for (nm in names(curves)) {
    stk <- NULL
    for (yr in years) {
      env_y <- get_env_for_year(yr, base_spat, dt_tmin, dt_tmax, dt_prec)
      vs    <- virtualspecies::generateSpFromFun(env_y, parameters = curves[[nm]], rescale = rescale)
      s     <- get_suit(vs)
      s     <- if (inherits(s, "SpatRaster")) s else terra::rast(s)
      names(s) <- paste0("y", yr)
      stk <- if (is.null(stk)) s else c(stk, s)
    }
    out[[nm]] <- stk
  }
  out
}

species_suitability <- simulate_three_species(
  env_stack_base,
  years   = 2000:2005,                 # or 2000:2020
  curves  = curve_list,
  dt_tmin = 0.30, dt_tmax = 0.30,      # ~ +1.5 °C in 5 years
  dt_prec = 1.0,                       # ~ +5 in 5 years
  rescale = TRUE                       # important, avoids collapse to ~0
)

plot(species_suitability$inc)   # SpatRaster: layers y2000..y2020 (increasing species)
plot(species_suitability$inc, col=rocket(100))

#-----


# boxplot

im.boxplot.layers(species_suitability$inc,
   density = TRUE,
   median_labels = TRUE,
   limits = c(0.01, 0.99),
   custom_colors = viridis::viridis(4, end = 0.5)
 )

Example: species distribution

Boxplot and kernel density

{r, echo=T, eval=F}
im.boxplot.layers(species_suitability$inc,
   density = TRUE,
   median_labels = TRUE,
   limits = c(0.01, 0.99),
   custom_colors = viridis::viridis(4, end = 0.5)
 )

3. Class-wise comparison

Outline

Spatial comparison

Class-wise comparison

Empirical example: drone imagery

{r, echo=T}
canale <- flip(rast("~/Documents/lectures_and_seminars/images/canale_aquila.JPG"))
im.plotRGB(canale, 1, 2, 3)

Empirical example: classified image

{r, echo=T, eval=T, eval=F}
classcanale <- im.classify(canale, num_clusters=4, seed=17)

Final kernel-density boxplot

{r, echo=T, eval=FALSE}
library(imageRy)
im.boxplot.classes(canale, classcanale, density=TRUE, layer=2, limits = c(0.01, 0.99), legend=T)

Methodological contribution

The framework provides a progressive workflow:

SpatRaster → im.ridgeline() → im.boxplot.layers() → im.classify() → im.boxplot.classes()

It integrates:

raster-native workflows

reproducible R code

Visualization and colorblindness

Rocchini et al. (2026). Under the mantra: ‘Make use of colorblind friendly graphs’. Environmetrics, e2877. https://doi.org/10.1002/env.2877

cblindplot package available at: https://github.com/ducciorocchini/cblindplot

Coda

Distribution-based visualization complements map-based analysis by showing information that maps often hide.

The framework helps users move from:

global distribution exploration

statistically informed layer comparison

spatially explicit class-wise interpretation

The main value is not a single plot, but a coherent exploratory workflow for raster data.
